stories.h: Okowa says he left Atiku for Tinubu because he has 'seen the light'
stories.p: Former Delta governor Ifeanyi Okowa, Atiku Abubakar's running mate in 2023, told an APC rally in Port Harcourt that he switched to backing President Tinubu because he has seen the light, crediting the government's fiscal reforms.
body: Former Delta State governor Ifeanyi Okowa has explained why he abandoned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to support President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 election.
## What he said

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Okowa reportedly said he had 'seen the light'. He argued that Tinubu inherited a country with foundations weakened by decades of mismanagement, and that the current administration was making tough but necessary decisions to fix them. He credited the government's fiscal reforms with increasing the revenue shared with states and local governments, saying the results could be seen in better project delivery and salary payments. He also compared Tinubu's record as Lagos governor with his performance as President, saying the same transformation was now happening across the country.
## Background

Okowa was Atiku's vice-presidential running mate on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) ticket in the 2023 election, which Tinubu won. He later left the PDP for the APC, following his successor in Delta, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori. Atiku is now the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), although a Federal High Court ruling last week voided his nomination, a decision the party has appealed. At the same rally, Tinubu questioned how Atiku built a university while he was vice-president, prompting a sharp reply from Atiku's campaign.
## What happens next
Atiku's campaign had not publicly responded to Okowa's remarks at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Okowa was Atiku's running mate in 2023.
He says Tinubu's reforms have boosted state revenues.
He spoke at an APC rally in Port Harcourt.

stories.h: Six Nigerians deported from the US arrive in Lagos
stories.p: The National Emergency Management Agency says it received six Nigerians deported from the United States at Lagos airport on 4 November. The five men and one woman were profiled by immigration officers and given resettlement support.
body: Six Nigerians deported from the United States have arrived in Lagos, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) says.
## What happened

In a statement on its X account on Sunday, 8 November 2026, NEMA said the five men and one woman, all adults, landed at the cargo terminal of Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Ikeja at about 10.13pm on Wednesday, 4 November, aboard a small chartered aircraft. NEMA's Lagos office received them in partnership with the US Consulate, the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Nigeria Immigration Service and an aviation services company. Immigration officers documented and profiled each returnee before clearing them, and NEMA said it coordinated support to help them resettle.
## Background

The deportations are part of the United States' wider crackdown on undocumented migrants under President Donald Trump, whose administration has carried out mass removals, often on chartered flights. Groups of Nigerians have been returned on several occasions over the past year. The agency did not give the reasons for the individual deportations. Trump this week named Stephen Miller, the architect of his deportation programme, as White House chief of staff.
## What happens next
NEMA said the federal government would continue to work with other agencies to manage the return of Nigerians from abroad in an orderly and dignified way.
more: Five men and one woman were deported.
They arrived in Lagos on 4 November.
NEMA says it is helping them resettle.

stories.h: All 10 passengers abducted from commercial bus in Ogun regain freedom, one suspected kidnapper killed
stories.p: All 10 passengers kidnapped from a commercial bus at Orita Fufu, Awa-Ijebu, Ogun State, on 3 November have been released unharmed, police say. One suspected kidnapper was killed in a follow-up operation, and an AK-47, ammunition and ₦1.37 million were recovered.
body: There is good news from Ogun State: all 10 passengers abducted from a commercial bus at Orita Fufu, Awa-Ijebu, have regained their freedom.
## Released unharmed
The passengers were taken on Tuesday, 3 November 2026. Police say they were released unharmed on the night of Saturday, 7 November, following sustained security pressure and intelligence-led efforts.
## Suspect killed, weapons and cash recovered
During a follow-up operation, police say one suspected kidnapper was killed. An AK-47 rifle, ammunition, ₦1.37 million in cash and a mobile phone were reportedly recovered.
Photos of the recovered items show bundles of naira notes, an AK-47 magazine and a mobile phone laid out on the ground in the bush.
## Questions still unanswered
Police have not said whether any ransom was paid for the passengers' release.
Reports also differ on whether any of the passengers was a serving or recently discharged member of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).
## Safe at last
The most important update is that all 10 passengers are alive and safely out of captivity, after five days that must have been terrifying for them and their families.
The incident is another reminder of the danger travellers face on Nigeria's highways, and of the need for security agencies to keep up pressure on kidnapping gangs.
## Over to you
What more should be done to make Nigeria's highways safe for travellers?
more: All 10 passengers were freed unharmed.
One suspected kidnapper was killed; an AK-47 and ₦1.37m were recovered.
Police have not said whether a ransom was paid.

stories.h: Flamingos get $50,000 reward, but no FIFA prize money for World Cup win
stories.p: Nigeria's U-17 world champions, the Flamingos, have received a $50,000 cash gift from a sponsor of the National Sports Commission at a reception in Rabat. FIFA does not pay prize money for the tournament because it is classed as a developmental competition.
body: Nigeria's Flamingos have received a $50,000 cash reward after winning the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, but the team will not receive any official prize money from FIFA.
## The reward

The gift was presented by Alhaji Saleh Ahmadu, a sponsor of the National Sports Commission (NSC), at a reception held in the team's honour in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday night, 7 November 2026, according to reports. The event was hosted by NSC chairman Shehu Dikko and director-general Bukola Olopade, and was also attended by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. The sponsor said the gift recognised the players' outstanding performance, commitment and determination.
## No FIFA prize money

FIFA classifies the U-17 Women's World Cup as a developmental tournament and does not attach official prize money to it, unlike the senior World Cups. That means the champions receive the trophy and medals but no payment from world football's governing body.
## How the final was won

The Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in the final on Saturday. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring when her looping effort slipped through the hands of Japan's goalkeeper, and Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the lead with a lob after a through ball from Esther Stephen. Japan's Fuki Ito pulled one back with ten minutes left, but Nigeria held on to become the first African winners of the tournament.
more: A sponsor gave the team $50,000 in Rabat.
FIFA pays no prize money for the U-17 Women's World Cup.
Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in the final.

stories.h: Tinubu to inaugurate sections of Kaduna–Kano and Kano–Maradi railways on 3 December
stories.p: President Tinubu will inaugurate completed sections of the Kaduna–Kano and Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway projects on 3 December, according to his campaign council. It says the Kaduna–Kano line is about 90% complete.
body: President Bola Tinubu has fixed 3 December 2026 for the inauguration of completed sections of two major railway projects in northern Nigeria.
## The projects

According to a statement on Sunday, 8 November 2026, by Dele Alake, spokesman of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, the 203-kilometre Kaduna–Kano Standard Gauge Railway is about 90 per cent complete, while the 400-kilometre Kano–Katsina–Maradi line, which will link Nigeria with the Republic of Niger, is about 70 per cent complete. The 190-kilometre Jaji-to-Kano segment of the Kaduna–Kano line and the 250-kilometre Dawanu–Kano–Kazaure–Daura–Katsina stretch of the Kano–Maradi line are due to be inaugurated on 3 December.
## Progress claims

The statement said that when Tinubu took office in 2023, the Kano–Maradi project was barely 5 per cent complete and the Kaduna–Kano line under 30 per cent. It said a federal inspection team led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Funso Adebiyi, recently assessed both corridors and carried out a test run. The figures come from the President's campaign and have not been independently verified.
## Background

The Kaduna–Kano line is part of the planned Lagos–Kano standard gauge railway, which already runs from Lagos to Ibadan and from Abuja to Kaduna. The Kano–Maradi project was started under former President Muhammadu Buhari.
## Why it matters
The inauguration will come just weeks before the 16 January 2027 presidential election, and infrastructure is a key part of the President's re-election campaign.
more: Sections of both lines open on 3 December.
The Kaduna–Kano line is said to be 90% complete.
The figures come from Tinubu's campaign.

stories.h: Lagos seals Surulere church over noise pollution after resident's complaint
stories.p: The Lagos State environment ministry has sealed All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere on Sunday morning after a resident complained online about noise. Commissioner Tokunbo Wahab said it will stay closed until further notice.
body: The Lagos State Government has sealed a church in Surulere over noise pollution.
## What happened

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, said on his X account on Sunday, 8 November 2026, that All Christians Gathering Ministry, located off Clegg Street in Surulere, had been shut and would remain closed until further notice. He said the action followed a complaint from a resident on X about noise from the church, and that officials investigated and confirmed the complaint was valid, finding the church in breach of environmental regulations. The sealing took place on Sunday morning.
## No exceptions
Wahab said the government would not soften its position on such violations, whether the offender is a religious body, a business or anyone else.
## Background

The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency has sealed many churches, mosques, hotels, clubs and event centres in recent years over noise pollution, often after complaints on social media. Wahab is known for responding publicly to residents' complaints online. Just this week, another Lagos resident cried out to the commissioner over noise from a church at midnight.

A resident had complained on X.
Commissioner Wahab says there will be no exceptions.

stories.h: VeryDarkMan challenges Zlatan Ibile to deny sending celebrities to beg him
stories.p: VeryDarkMan has dared Zlatan Ibile to publicly deny that he secretly sent celebrities to plead with him over their ongoing feud, accusing the singer of acting tough in public while trying to settle the matter behind the scenes. He has threatened to name the celebrities.
body: Social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) has continued his public exchange with singer Zlatan Ibile, daring him to openly deny claims that he secretly sent celebrities to plead with VDM over their ongoing disagreement.
## "Just come out and say it's a lie"

Speaking partly in Pidgin, VDM said, in effect: "It's been over 24 hours since I dared Zlatan to come out and say I'm lying that he sent people to beg me. He acts like a hard guy in public, but does something else behind the scenes."
"Just come out and say it's a lie, simple! Let me call out the names of the celebrities you sent. If they deny it too, then you'll see what my next post will be."

He added that he was only holding back out of respect for Zlatan's parents: "It's because your mother and father are involved. We still respect parents here. If not, everyone would already know that you have no class."
## Tough in public, soft in private?
VDM claims Zlatan is acting tough in public while making moves behind the scenes to settle the matter, and has threatened to name the celebrities he says were sent if Zlatan stays silent.

The feud began after a video of Davido singing a line from Zlatan's song INFERNO at Zlatan's wedding welcome party in Morocco, a lyric VDM believes was aimed at him. VDM then warned Zlatan that he would "learn the hard way".
## Allegations, not facts
For now, these remain VeryDarkMan's claims. Zlatan has not responded publicly, and his silence does not confirm them.
## Over to you
Will Zlatan respond, or will he let VDM keep controlling the conversation?
more: VDM says Zlatan secretly sent celebrities to beg him.
He has threatened to name them.
Zlatan has not responded publicly.

stories.h: "You're becoming very noisy, 'money na water'!": Umahi fires back at Cubana Chief Priest, questions his wealth and contributions to society
stories.p: Works Minister David Umahi has hit back at Cubana Chief Priest, weeks after the celebrity businessman called him the second-worst minister from the South-East. Umahi mocked his famous "money na water" catchphrase and asked how many people he has given scholarships.
body: "You're becoming very noisy. Money na water. How much do you have? Have you ever seen Dangote saying, 'I have money,' or Otedola saying that he's rich? Money speaks for itself. It's not by saying money na water. What have you done? How many people have you given scholarships?"

Those were the strong words of Nigeria's Minister of Works, David Umahi, as he fired back at Cubana Chief Priest, weeks after the celebrity businessman described him as the second-worst minister from the South-East.
## "Money speaks for itself"

The criticism clearly did not go down well with the former Ebonyi State governor, who has now turned the conversation towards wealth, public conduct and what rich people are doing to improve the lives of others.
Umahi questioned the constant public display of wealth, particularly the expression "money na water" (meaning money flows like water), which Cubana Chief Priest is widely known for.

He pointed to two of Nigeria's richest businessmen, Aliko Dangote and Femi Otedola, and asked whether Nigerians regularly hear them announcing how much money they have. For Umahi, genuine wealth should speak through achievements, investments and contributions to society, not constant declarations on social media.
## The scholarship question
The line that stands out most is his question: "How many people have you given scholarships?"
That question takes the argument beyond who has more money. It raises a different issue entirely: what impact are wealthy Nigerians making in the lives of ordinary people?
## Two different conversations

Cubana Chief Priest has every right to criticise a public officeholder, and Umahi, as a serving minister, is equally entitled to respond. But criticism of a minister's performance is ultimately best answered with evidence of work done, projects completed and results delivered.

That is what makes this exchange interesting. Umahi is questioning Cubana Chief Priest's display of wealth, while the original criticism was about Umahi's performance as Minister of Works. These are two different conversations, and Nigerians will have their opinions on both.
## Over to you

Does Cubana Chief Priest need to prove how many people he has helped before he can criticise a serving minister? Or should Umahi focus on defending his performance in office rather than questioning another man's wealth?
more: Cubana Chief Priest called Umahi the second-worst South-East minister.
Umahi mocked his 'money na water' catchphrase.

stories.h: Bandits reportedly kill 12 members of one family in Zamfara village attack
stories.p: Twelve members of the same family were reportedly killed when bandits set fire to the building where they had taken refuge during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun LGA, Zamfara State. Other residents were said to have been kidnapped.
body: Twelve members of one family have reportedly been killed in an attack by bandits on a village in Zamfara State.
## What happened

The attack took place late on Saturday, 7 November 2026, in Gidan Taba village, Dosara Birnin Kaya ward, in Maradun Local Government Area, according to residents. A resident said the head of the family had gathered his relatives into a single room to try to stop them from being kidnapped. When the attackers found the family and they refused to come out, the bandits reportedly set the building on fire, and all 12 people inside died. An unknown number of other residents were reportedly abducted during the raid. The victims were buried according to Islamic rites on Sunday morning.
## Official response
The police and the Zamfara State Government had not publicly commented on the attack at the time of writing.
## Background

Zamfara is one of the states worst affected by banditry in Nigeria's North-West, with armed groups carrying out killings, mass kidnappings and attacks on farming communities. Last week, bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers on the Sokoto–Gusau road, reportedly killing and abducting some of them. Security forces have carried out repeated operations in the state's forests, but attacks on villages continue.
more: Twelve family members were reportedly killed.

The attack happened in Maradun LGA.

stories.h: Amaechi warns court ruling against ADC could trigger unrest if mishandled
stories.p: ADC vice-presidential candidate Rotimi Amaechi has warned that the court judgment removing the party's leadership and voiding Atiku Abubakar's nomination could lead to serious unrest, even civil war, if the dispute is not properly managed.
body: Rotimi Amaechi, the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has warned that the court ruling against the party's leadership could cause serious unrest if it is not handled carefully.
## What he said

In comments reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Amaechi said the judgment that nullified the party's leadership and the process that produced Atiku Abubakar as presidential candidate could lead to civil war if the dispute is not properly managed. He did not set out in detail how he believed the crisis should be resolved.
## The ruling

On Thursday, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that the national working committee led by former Senate President David Mark was invalid. The judgment also nullified the emergence of former Interior Minister Rauf Aregbesola as national secretary, and decisions taken by the Mark-led leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as candidate. The court directed INEC not to recognise decisions taken at the party's national executive committee meeting of 27 July 2025. The suit was filed by Nafiu Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the party.
## Background

The ADC has appealed the judgment and asked INEC not to act on it until the appeal is heard. Atiku has vowed to stay in the race and accused the government of using the courts against the opposition. Amaechi, a former Rivers governor and transport minister, this week also said former President Muhammadu Buhari had promised in writing to back him in 2022.
## What happens next
Attention is now on the Court of Appeal and on how INEC responds before the presidential election on 16 January 2027.
more: Amaechi says the ruling could cause unrest if mishandled.
The court voided Atiku's nomination last week.
The ADC has appealed.

stories.h: Gift Orban overtakes injured Osimhen in Turkish league scoring race
stories.p: Super Eagles striker Gift Orban scored his 10th Turkish Süper Lig goal of the season for Amedspor, moving one ahead of the injured Victor Osimhen in the race for the Golden Boot, though Amedspor lost 4-3 to Galatasaray.
body: Nigerian striker Gift Orban has moved ahead of Victor Osimhen in the race to be top scorer in Turkey's Süper Lig.
## The goal

Orban scored his 10th league goal of the season for Amedspor in their 4-3 defeat away to Galatasaray, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026. After a quiet first half, the former Lyon striker headed home from close range from a cross by substitute Furkan Soyalp. Another Nigerian, Yira Sor, also scored for Amedspor after coming off the bench, but Galatasaray held on to win.
## The scoring race

The goal took Orban to 10 goals and five assists in 11 league appearances, one more goal than Osimhen, who has nine goals and three assists in eight league games. Osimhen missed the match after having knee surgery on Saturday to remove a loose body from his left knee, and is expected to be out for at least three weeks.
## Background

Orban joined Amedspor on loan in the summer transfer window. He made his name at Belgian club Gent, where he scored freely, before moving to Lyon. Osimhen, the 2023 African Player of the Year, has been out of action since the Champions League win over Stuttgart. Both are Super Eagles strikers, and with Osimhen ruled out of the AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania this month, Orban's form will interest Nigeria's coaching staff.
more: Orban has 10 league goals this season.

stories.h: Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.p: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while using unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels were not named. The incident comes days after US strikes on Iranian targets.
body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
## What Iran said

In a statement carried by Iran's state news agency on Sunday, 8 November 2026, the Guards said one tanker struck a mine in the eastern part of the strait and the other elsewhere in the waterway, while trying to cross using routes not authorised by Tehran. The statement did not name the vessels or give their nationalities, and accused them of violations including switching off their navigation and tracking systems. There was no independent confirmation of the incidents or of any casualties.
## Background

Iran has sharply restricted shipping through the strait since a war began in late February, requiring ships to follow routes it has approved. The United States responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has helped tankers pass through the waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil. Iran has reported several ships catching fire in the strait in recent weeks. The incident comes days after US forces struck an Iranian air defence site on Qeshm Island, an operation President Donald Trump described as minor.
## Why it matters
Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz affects global oil supply and prices, which in turn affect Nigeria's oil revenue and the cost of imported fuel.

stories.h: Saidi Balogun hits back at critics over his campaigning for Tinubu
stories.p: Nollywood actor Saidi Balogun has responded to online attacks over videos of him hosting campaign rallies for President Tinubu, urging people to respect others' political choices.
body: Nollywood actor Saidi Balogun has responded to criticism over his open support for President Bola Tinubu's re-election bid.
## What happened

The actor had shared videos on social media showing him hosting campaign rallies for the President in different parts of the country, which drew strong criticism from some social media users. In a response reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Balogun refused to back down, urging critics to allow people to hold different political views without being attacked.
## Background

Balogun is a veteran actor, producer and director in the Yoruba film industry. He is one of several entertainers who have appeared at Tinubu's campaign events in recent weeks, alongside others such as actress Eniola Badmus, who also posted a video this week explaining why she believes the President deserves a second term.
## The wider debate

The involvement of entertainers in the 2027 campaigns has divided opinion online. Some argue that public figures have every right to back the candidates they choose, while others say supporting the government amounts to endorsing economic hardship. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Balogun has hosted rallies for Tinubu.

stories.h: Tony Elumelu celebrates daughter's Oxford master's degree
stories.p: Billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu has celebrated his eldest daughter, Ogechukwu, on earning a Master of Science degree from the University of Oxford while also completing a law conversion course.
body: Billionaire businessman and philanthropist Tony Elumelu has celebrated his eldest daughter, Ogechukwu, after she earned a master's degree from the University of Oxford.
## What happened

In a social media post on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Elumelu shared a video from the graduation ceremony, saying his daughter had achieved two major milestones: a Master of Science degree from Oxford and the completion of a law conversion course. The video showed the family celebrating together.
## Background

Ogechukwu, also known as Tamara-Marie Oge Elumelu, is the daughter of Tony Elumelu and his wife, Dr Awele Elumelu. She previously graduated with honours from the London School of Economics, where she studied politics and philosophy. Tony Elumelu is the chairman of Heirs Holdings and the United Bank for Africa (UBA), and founder of the Tony Elumelu Foundation, which supports young African entrepreneurs. He made headlines recently with a gift at singer Zlatan Ibile's wedding.
## How people reacted
The post drew congratulatory messages from followers and public figures.
more: Ogechukwu Elumelu earned an MSc from Oxford.
She also completed a law conversion course.

stories.h: Nkem Owoh denies saying Yoruba founded Nollywood, credits them with pioneering films
stories.p: Veteran actor Nkem Owoh, known as Osuofia, has said on a popular interview show that he never claimed the Yoruba founded Nollywood, pointing out that the word did not exist when he started acting, but credited Yoruba filmmakers such as Hubert Ogunde with pioneering the tradition.
body: Veteran Nollywood actor Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has addressed comments attributed to him about who founded Nigeria's film industry.
## What he said

Speaking on the YouTube interview show 'Curiosity Made Me Ask', hosted by content creator Isbae U, in an episode uploaded on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Owoh rejected reports that he had said the Yoruba people started Nollywood rather than the Igbo. He explained that the word 'Nollywood' did not even exist when he and his colleagues first began making films. However, he said Yoruba filmmakers had indeed pioneered the home-video tradition in Nigeria, giving particular credit to the late theatre and film pioneer Hubert Ogunde. When the host jokingly suggested Ogunde might have been Igbo, Owoh insisted that he was Yoruba.
## The wider debate

The question of who built Nollywood has been debated for years. In August 2026, the late actor Francis Duru argued that Igbo businesspeople were the real architects of the home-video boom of the 1990s and early 2000s, while accepting that the Yoruba film community had become more dominant through stronger organisation. Owoh was reported at the time to have pointed out that Yoruba filmmakers were active in theatre and film long before the video boom. Duru died in October 2026.
## Background

Owoh is one of Nollywood's best-loved comic actors, famous for the 'Osuofia in London' films and the song 'I Go Chop Your Dollar'. 'Curiosity Made Me Ask' is one of Nigeria's most popular celebrity interview shows.
more: Owoh says he never claimed the Yoruba founded Nollywood.

stories.h: CBN sets ₦15bn capital rule for dollar-backed stablecoins in new crypto rules
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has set minimum capital of ₦10 billion for naira-backed stablecoin issuers and ₦15 billion for those offering dollar or other foreign-currency tokens, under new rules for crypto operators. Other crypto service providers will need ₦1 billion.
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced tougher rules for cryptocurrency and stablecoin businesses, including minimum capital requirements of up to ₦15 billion.
## The new requirements

Under the regulations, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, issuers of naira-backed stablecoins must have at least ₦10 billion in paid-up capital, while operators offering tokens backed by foreign currencies, such as dollar-pegged stablecoins, will need ₦15 billion. Other virtual asset service providers, including digital wallet, payment, transfer and custody businesses, must have at least ₦1 billion. The CBN said it may demand more capital from larger or riskier operators.
## Licensing and foreign firms

The rules make it illegal for individuals or companies to issue, exchange, distribute or facilitate regulated virtual assets in Nigeria without CBN approval. Foreign operators targeting Nigerian customers must incorporate and obtain licences locally, regardless of approvals elsewhere. Companies already licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will face extra capital requirements if they offer services under the CBN's oversight, while digital assets classed as securities will remain under SEC supervision. The rules also set standards for reserve management and consumer protection.
## Deadlines and fines

The regulations, released on Friday, give existing operators 30 days to register with the CBN, 60 days to begin submitting supervisory reports and 180 days to complete licence applications. Operators can continue at their current scale during the transition, but those who miss the deadline must suspend operations until licensed. Firms operating without approval face fines starting at ₦100 million.
## Background

Nigeria has one of the world's largest communities of cryptocurrency users. The CBN banned banks from dealing with crypto firms in 2021 before lifting the restriction in 2023, and the SEC has since moved to register and regulate crypto exchanges. Stablecoins, which are designed to keep a steady value linked to a currency such as the dollar, are widely used by Nigerians for savings and payments.
more: Dollar-backed stablecoin issuers need ₦15 billion in capital.
Naira-backed issuers need ₦10 billion.
Foreign operators must be licensed locally.

stories.h: MultiChoice shuts down GOtv Stream app months after closing Showmax
stories.p: MultiChoice has discontinued its GOtv Stream mobile app, telling users to go back to their decoders, without giving a reason. It is the latest change since French group Canal+ took over the company, following the closure of Showmax in April.
body: MultiChoice has shut down its GOtv Stream app, which allowed subscribers to watch selected GOtv channels on phones and tablets.
## What happened

A notice on the GOtv Stream website, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, confirmed the closure and directed customers back to their television decoders. The app has also been removed from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store; app-tracking data showed the Android version was removed on 21 October. Before the closure, it offered live channels, catch-up programmes and offline downloads, depending on the subscription package. MultiChoice has not given a reason for the shutdown or announced a replacement.
## Background

GOtv Stream launched in Nigeria on 1 December 2023 as part of MultiChoice's effort to let subscribers watch TV away from their living rooms. The closure is the latest change since French media group Canal+ took control of MultiChoice in a deal valued at about $2 billion, which became unconditional in September 2025. MultiChoice announced in March 2026 that it would close its Showmax streaming service, citing heavy losses, and Showmax shut down in April, with subscribers directed to DStv Stream. The company has also recently dropped the Africa Magic Family channel after 12 years.
more: The GOtv Stream app has been discontinued.
No reason or replacement has been announced.
Showmax closed in April.

stories.h: Opeyemi Falegan apologises to Nkechi Blessing on TikTok Live years after split
stories.p: Ekiti politician Opeyemi Falegan has publicly apologised to actress Nkechi Blessing Sunday during a TikTok Live session, years after their messy 2022 break-up. Nkechi said his past remarks about her were still being used against her.
body: Ekiti politician Opeyemi Falegan has publicly apologised to Nollywood actress Nkechi Blessing Sunday, years after their much-discussed break-up.
## What happened

The apology came during a TikTok Live session on Saturday, 7 November 2026, in which the former couple spoke face to face online about their 2022 separation. Nkechi made it clear that she wanted a genuine apology, reminding Falegan that remarks he made about her during a social media live session years ago were still circulating and being used against her. She also said that despite their fallout, she had defended him in comment sections when people criticised him.
## Falegan's response

Falegan apologised and said he had grown since their split, urging both of them to let the past go. He also spoke about what he described as emotional unavailability and temperament issues on both sides that made the relationship difficult.
## Background

Nkechi Blessing is a popular actress and producer known for her outspoken personality on social media. Her relationship with Falegan was widely publicised before it ended in 2022 amid public exchanges online. The actress was also recently in the news after confronting comedian Carter Efe and his girlfriend.
## How people reacted
Fans were divided, with some praising the two for making peace and others questioning why Nkechi chose to revisit the matter in public.
more: Falegan apologised during a TikTok Live.
The couple split in 2022.
Fans were divided over the public reunion.

stories.h: Obi asks Tinubu to account for subsidy savings and over $100bn in loans
stories.p: NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged President Tinubu to explain what his government has done with the ₦15.8 trillion reportedly saved from fuel subsidy removal and more than $100 billion in borrowing, a day after Tinubu criticised Obi's record in Anambra.
body: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has called on President Bola Tinubu to account for money saved from the removal of the fuel subsidy and from government borrowing.
## What Obi said

In a statement on his X account on Saturday, 7 November 2026, titled 'Good Day, Mr President: Nigerians Deserve Accountability', Obi said the large sums flowing into government coffers, including higher tax revenues, should be producing clear improvements in Nigerians' daily lives. He urged the President to visit the remaining 33 states he has not yet toured, spend time with the people and explain what his administration had done with the ₦15.8 trillion he said had been saved from subsidy removal, the more than $100 billion he said had been borrowed, and increased revenue from taxes.
## The background to the exchange

Obi's statement came a day after Tinubu, speaking in Akwa Ibom, criticised the former Anambra governor's record on erosion in the state. At a reception in Uyo the same day, Tinubu said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms and that Nigeria would never go back to the subsidy. Vice-President Kashim Shettima also told an APC rally in Uyo that Obi had run himself out of the race.
## The figures

Obi did not give a breakdown of how he arrived at the figures. The World Bank reported this week that Nigeria's total external debt, including private-sector debt, rose to about $145 billion in 2025. The government says its borrowing is needed to fund infrastructure and that its reforms have saved the economy from collapse.
## What happens next
The Presidency had not publicly responded to Obi's statement at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Obi cited ₦15.8 trillion in subsidy savings.
He said Tinubu had borrowed over $100 billion.
The statement followed Tinubu's remarks in Akwa Ibom.

stories.h: Van Vicker says viral photos of him with Regina Daniels are AI-generated
stories.p: Ghanaian actor Van Vicker has dismissed viral photos appearing to show him with Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, saying they were created with artificial intelligence and that the two have not been in contact for more than a decade.
body: Ghanaian actor Van Vicker has dismissed viral images appearing to show him with Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, saying they were generated using artificial intelligence.
## The photos

According to reports on Sunday, 8 November 2026, one of the images showed Van Vicker carrying a much younger Regina Daniels, while another placed him beside her during what looked like her recent birthday photoshoot. The pictures spread widely online and caused a stir among fans of both actors.
## What he said
Van Vicker said neither image was real, and that he and Regina Daniels had not been in contact for well over a decade. He spoke out quickly to stop the rumours from spreading further.
## Background

Van Vicker is one of the best-known Ghanaian actors in Nollywood and has starred in many Nigerian films since the mid-2000s. Regina Daniels, who began acting as a child, has been in the news recently, including a public clash with journalist Kemi Olunloyo, and new videos from the mansion of her husband, Senator Ned Nwoko, have also drawn attention online. The case is the latest example of AI-generated images of celebrities spreading on social media and being mistaken for real photos.
more: Van Vicker says the photos were made with AI.
He says he has not been in contact with Regina for over a decade.
The images spread widely online.

stories.h: Petrol prices at Lagos depots rise by up to ₦60 a litre as diesel falls
stories.p: Depot prices of petrol in Lagos rose by as much as ₦60 per litre this week, with several depots moving from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280, while diesel prices fell. The rise came despite a drop in global crude oil prices.
body: Petrol prices at major fuel depots in Lagos rose by as much as ₦60 per litre this week, while diesel prices fell, according to market data reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026.
## The figures

Between Monday and Friday, the average petrol price across seven comparable depots in Lagos rose by about ₦41 per litre, while diesel fell by about ₦33. Some of the biggest increases were recorded at African Terminal, Integrated and A.A. Rano, which each raised their prices from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280 per litre. Aiteo raised its price by ₦56 to ₦1,277, Rain Oil by ₦55 to ₦1,280 and Nipco by ₦29 to ₦1,279, while MRS Tincan cut its price by ₦30 to ₦1,280. Similar movements were seen at depots in Warri and Port Harcourt.
## Crude prices fell

The increases came even though international crude oil prices fell during the week, with Brent crude reportedly dropping by almost 5 per cent. Domestic supply conditions and marketers' costs also affect local prices.
## Background

Depot prices are what marketers pay before selling to motorists, so changes usually feed through to filling-station prices within days. Petrol prices are now set by the market after the removal of the fuel subsidy in 2023, and have fluctuated with competition between the Dangote refinery, NNPC and importers. President Bola Tinubu said in Uyo this week that the government will never return to the subsidy. Cooking gas prices have also reportedly risen to about ₦1,900 per kilogram.
## Cooking gas also up

Cooking gas prices have also risen. Retail prices reached about ₦1,800 per kilogram in Lagos and Ogun states after depot prices rose from ₦1,100 to as much as ₦1,445 per kilogram, an increase of about 31 per cent, according to reports on Sunday. Most depots were selling at ₦1,445, while Dangote's depot was selling at ₦1,150. At ₦1,800 per kilogram, refilling a 12.5kg cylinder costs about ₦22,500.
## What it means
Motorists may see higher pump prices in the coming days, while businesses that rely on diesel could get some relief.
more: Some depots raised petrol from ₦1,220 to ₦1,280 a litre.
Diesel prices fell during the week.
Global crude prices dropped.

stories.h: "Political immaturity": Why attack Peter Obi when you are not contesting against him? Rep Ogene questions Umahi, Soludo
stories.p: Rep Afam Victor Ogene has accused Works Minister David Umahi and Anambra Governor Charles Soludo of "political immaturity" for repeatedly attacking Peter Obi, pointing out that South-West leaders are not attacking Governor Seyi Makinde over his own presidential ambition.
body: A member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Afam Victor Ogene, has questioned what he sees as growing political hostility towards Peter Obi, the NDC presidential candidate and Labour Party candidate in 2023, particularly from prominent politicians in the South-East.
## A tale of two regions
Ogene drew attention to what he described as a striking difference between the political atmosphere in the South-West and the South-East ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to him, governors and ministers from the South-West are not publicly attacking Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde over his perceived presidential ambition, even though he could challenge President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

In the South-East, however, he questioned why Minister of Works David Umahi and Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo keep directing criticism at Obi, even though neither of them is contesting the presidency against him.

"Southwest governors and ministers are not attacking Seyi Makinde for contesting against Tinubu, but Umahi and Soludo keep attacking Peter Obi even when none of them is contesting. That's political immaturity," Ogene said.
## Rivalry or genuine criticism?
His remarks raise a wider question about the nature of political rivalry in Nigeria, particularly in the South-East, where disagreements among prominent figures often attract public attention.
Why should politicians who are not directly competing against Obi appear more concerned about his political future than those who may eventually face him at the ballot box?
For Ogene, the issue goes beyond ordinary disagreement. His criticism suggests some leaders may be letting personal rivalry and party differences overshadow mutual respect.

The comparison with the South-West is particularly interesting. Despite belonging to different parties and having different presidential interests, leaders in that region have often managed their disagreements while keeping working relationships.
## Obi is not above scrutiny

Every politician has the right to criticise another, and Obi, as an active national figure, is equally open to public scrutiny. Umahi has recently questioned whether Obi is better than him or Pius Anyim, while Soludo has backed President Tinubu. Ogene's argument raises the question of whether such criticism is based on genuine policy differences or unnecessary rivalry.
Political disagreements are unavoidable in a democracy, but how leaders handle them says a great deal about their political maturity.
## Over to you
Do you agree with Hon. Ogene that South-East leaders are unnecessarily attacking Peter Obi, or are Umahi and Soludo simply exercising their right to criticise a fellow politician?
more: Ogene called the attacks on Obi 'political immaturity'.
He compared it with South-West leaders' silence on Makinde.

stories.h: "I established my university before becoming Vice-President": Atiku fires back at Tinubu
stories.p: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has responded to President Bola Tinubu's questions about how he built a university while in government, saying his journey into education began in 1993 with ABTI Academy, six years before he took office, and that his business record is open to scrutiny.
body: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has responded to President Bola Tinubu over questions about his investment in education, insisting that the foundation of his educational institution was laid long before he became Vice-President.
## Atiku's response
Atiku, who served as Vice-President from 1999 to 2007, said the suggestion that he established a university with resources acquired while in public office was misleading.
According to him, his journey into education began in 1993, when he established ABTI Academy, six years before he took office as Vice-President under former President Olusegun Obasanjo.
He made the clarification after remarks attributed to President Tinubu questioning how he was able to set up a university while serving in government.
## Why the dates matter

Atiku maintained that his investment in education was part of his business activities before he entered the country's second-highest office. By the time he became Vice-President in May 1999, he says, he had already begun building what would eventually grow into a major private institution.

That institution later became the American University of Nigeria (AUN) in Yola, Adamawa State. The university itself was established in the mid-2000s, during his time as Vice-President, which is why questions about its funding and expansion continue to come up.
Atiku also insisted that his business activities and investments are open to public scrutiny, and that anyone genuinely interested in the source and history of his wealth can examine his record.
## A growing rivalry
The exchange adds another chapter to the rivalry between President Tinubu and the former Vice-President, two prominent figures whose differences have shaped several national debates.

Beyond the personal disagreement, the controversy raises a question Nigerians have long asked of their leaders: how did those who held public office acquire their wealth, and can they give a clear account of their investments?

The fact that an educational project began before someone took office does not, on its own, settle every question about its funding or later expansion. Those questions would require documentary evidence and a proper look at the institution's financial history.
## The road to 2027
As activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather pace, exchanges like this between leading political figures are likely to attract even more attention.
For now, Atiku has made his position clear: his educational investment began in 1993, well before he became Vice-President, and he is prepared to have his business record examined.
## Over to you
Should Nigerian politicians be required to publicly explain how they funded their major investments, regardless of when those investments began?
more: Atiku says he founded ABTI Academy in 1993, before becoming VP.
Tinubu had questioned how he built a university while in office.
Atiku says his business record is open to scrutiny.

stories.h: "Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022, I regret listening to him": Rotimi Amaechi
stories.p: Former Rivers governor and ex-Transport Minister Rotimi Amaechi has reportedly said the late President Muhammadu Buhari promised him the APC presidential ticket in 2022, a promise he now regrets believing. Amaechi went on to lose the primary to Bola Tinubu.
body: Former Rivers State Governor and ex-Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi has reportedly expressed regret over his decision to trust former President Muhammadu Buhari during the race for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket in 2022.
## The promise
According to the statement attributed to Amaechi, Buhari had promised him the party's presidential ticket, a promise he now regrets believing.

The claim raises fresh questions about the political arrangements and behind-the-scenes discussions that took place before the APC primary that eventually produced Bola Ahmed Tinubu as the party's candidate.
Buhari died in July 2025, so he is no longer able to respond to Amaechi's account.
## How the 2022 race played out

Amaechi was among the prominent politicians who contested the ticket in 2022. Despite being a serving minister in Buhari's government and a close associate of the President, he lost the primary to Tinubu.
As the sitting President and leader of the ruling party at the time, Buhari's influence was considerable, although the final decision rested with the party's delegates.
## Loyalty without reward
For Amaechi, the disappointment appears to go beyond losing an election. His comments suggest he believed he had received an assurance from someone whose word carried enormous political weight.
That points to one of the oldest lessons in Nigerian politics: loyalty does not always guarantee reward.

Amaechi served under Buhari for nearly seven years as Minister of Transportation, and he was one of the key figures who helped build the coalition that brought the APC to power in 2015. Yet when his chance came to seek the presidency, things did not turn out as he had apparently expected.
## The questions that remain
Did Buhari actually make such a commitment, and if he did, what happened between that promise and the primary?
Was Amaechi politically outplayed, or did he place too much confidence in a promise that was never guaranteed?
Whatever the answer, his regret offers another glimpse into the complicated world of Nigerian party politics, where today's allies can have very different interests when power is at stake.
## Over to you
Do you believe Buhari promised Amaechi the ticket, and was he right to trust him?
more: Amaechi says Buhari promised him the APC ticket in 2022.
He lost the APC primary to Bola Tinubu.

stories.h: Crowd erupts in 'Obi' chants as Deputy Speaker Ben Kalu campaigns for Tinubu at Item Okpi festival in Aba
stories.p: As Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu urged the crowd at the Item Okpi cultural festival in Aba to back President Tinubu, sections of the audience reportedly broke into loud chants of "Obi! Obi! Obi!", even as he declared, "On your mandate we shall stand."
body: What was meant to be a moment of political mobilisation for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu reportedly took an unexpected turn at the Item Okpi cultural festival in Aba, Abia State, when members of the crowd began chanting the name of Peter Obi.
## "Obi! Obi! Obi!"

The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, was addressing a large gathering at the cultural event when he turned to national politics and began appealing to the people to support President Tinubu.
The response from sections of the audience was not what he appeared to be hoping for. As Kalu spoke in support of the President, loud chants of "Obi! Obi! Obi!" reportedly rose from the crowd.

Even when the Deputy Speaker repeated the familiar declaration, "On your mandate we shall stand," the chants continued, creating an unusual scene in which the politician's message and the crowd's response seemed to be moving in opposite directions.
## Why it matters
The moment has drawn attention because of Abia State's political significance and the continuing debate about the popularity of Nigeria's major political figures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party and is now the NDC presidential candidate, continues to command a strong following in sections of the electorate, particularly in the South-East.
For Kalu, an influential APC politician from Abia State, the incident highlights the challenge of promoting the ruling party's candidate in a region where political loyalties remain divided.
## A cultural festival turned political

Chants from a crowd at a cultural gathering are not a scientific measure of how a state or region will vote. But public reactions like this can still offer a glimpse into the political conversations happening among ordinary Nigerians.

What makes this incident stand out is the setting. The gathering was mainly a cultural celebration, yet it became a scene of competing political expressions once the Deputy Speaker raised the subject of presidential support.
## Over to you

Were the chants simply a spontaneous reaction from enthusiastic Obi supporters, or a sign of wider political sentiment in the area? One thing is clear: Ben Kalu was talking about Tinubu, but some voices in the crowd wanted to talk about Obi.
more: Ben Kalu urged the Aba crowd to support Tinubu.
Sections of the crowd chanted 'Obi! Obi! Obi!'

stories.h: Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win Nigeria's first U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.p: Nigeria's Flamingos have won the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, beating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored, making Nigeria the first African team to win the tournament.
body: Nigeria's under-17 women's team, the Flamingos, are world champions after beating Japan 2-1 in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday, 7 November 2026.
## The match

Awawu Bashiru gave Nigeria the lead in the 39th minute at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, and Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the advantage two minutes after half-time, in the 47th minute. Japan pulled a goal back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to claim the trophy.
## History made

The victory makes Nigeria the first African country to win the competition, and gives the country its first FIFA world title in women's football at any level. Before this tournament, the Flamingos' best finish was third place in 2022. They reached the final by beating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final, a match in which Bashiru also scored twice, while Japan beat North Korea on penalties in their semi-final.
## Background

Japan came into the final as one of the strongest teams in youth women's football, having won the tournament in 2014 and finished as runners-up in 2010 and 2016. CAF president Patrice Motsepe had travelled to Rabat to watch the final after praising the Flamingos for making Africa proud. Before the match, captain Harmony Chidi said the team was determined to bring the trophy home.
## What happens next
The win comes as the senior Super Eagles prepare for their AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania next week.
more: Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat.
Bashiru and Umejiaku scored for the Flamingos.
Nigeria are the first African winners of the tournament.

stories.h: EFCC chairman says Adeboye ordered return of billions donated to RCCG project
stories.p: EFCC chairman Ola Olukoyede says RCCG General Overseer Enoch Adeboye ordered the refund of billions of naira donated to a church project within 24 hours of learning the money was proceeds of crime. He did not name the donor or the project.
body: The chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Ola Olukoyede, says Pastor Enoch Adeboye, General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), ordered the return of billions of naira donated to a church project after learning that the money came from crime.
## What he said

Speaking to RCCG workers early on Saturday, 7 November 2026, at a meeting held ahead of the church's annual Holy Ghost Congress, Olukoyede said Adeboye directed that the money be refunded within 24 hours of being told where it came from. He praised the pastor for acting quickly. According to reports, he did not name the donor, say which project the money was meant for, or give the exact amount.
## Warning to churches

Olukoyede, who is himself an ordained pastor, said Adeboye had invited him to speak to the workers about financial accountability and keeping transparent records. He expressed concern about a growing number of cases involving church leaders in financial crimes and about allegations linked to contract awards for church projects.
## Background
The RCCG is one of Nigeria's largest churches, and its Holy Ghost Congress draws huge crowds to the Redemption Camp on the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway every December.
more: Adeboye reportedly ordered a refund within 24 hours.
The EFCC did not name the donor or project.
Olukoyede spoke ahead of the Holy Ghost Congress.

stories.h: Ebonyi women parade man in wheelbarrow over alleged repeated beating of his wife
stories.p: Women in Ishiagu, Ivo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State, have reportedly paraded a man around the community in a wheelbarrow over claims that he repeatedly beat his wife. The unusual punishment has sparked debate about domestic violence and community justice.
body: Women in Ishiagu community, Ivo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State, have reportedly taken an unusual step to show their anger over domestic violence, publicly parading a man accused of repeatedly beating his wife.
## Pushed around in a wheelbarrow

According to reports circulating online, the women placed the man in a wheelbarrow and pushed him around the community, apparently determined to make an example of him over his alleged treatment of his wife.
Photos show a large group of women surrounding the man, who sits in the wheelbarrow in a yellow T-shirt as several women push and guide it along a dirt path, with one carrying a calabash.
## "Enough is enough"
The incident has drawn attention because of the unusual punishment the women chose. They appeared to have reached a point where they could no longer tolerate the alleged abuse.

In many communities, domestic violence is still treated as a private family matter, and victims are sometimes encouraged to endure abuse for the sake of their marriage. The women of Ishiagu reportedly decided that enough was enough.
## Justice or humiliation?
Their action raises an important question about how communities should respond when a woman is repeatedly subjected to violence in her own home.
Many people may applaud the women for standing up against domestic abuse. Others may question whether publicly humiliating an accused person, who has not been tried, is the right approach.
The full circumstances of the incident, including the man's side of the story and whether the authorities have stepped in, remain unclear.
## Over to you
Do you support what the women of Ishiagu reportedly did, or should they have handed the man over to the police instead? Was this community justice, or public humiliation taken too far?
more: The incident reportedly happened in Ishiagu, Ebonyi State.
The man is accused of repeatedly beating his wife.
It is unclear whether the police have intervened.

stories.h: Tinubu asks how Atiku built a university while he was vice-president
stories.p: At an APC rally in Port Harcourt, President Tinubu said he was cleaning up a mess created by people complaining about hunger, naming Atiku Abubakar, and questioned how the ADC candidate built a university while in office.
body: President Bola Tinubu has launched one of his sharpest attacks yet on Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
## What he said

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Tinubu dismissed critics who point to economic hardship under his government, saying he was cleaning up the mess left by those who came before him and that Atiku was one of them. He also questioned how Atiku had built a university while he was vice-president, a remark widely seen as raising questions about how the former vice-president acquired his wealth while in public office.
## Background

Atiku served as vice-president from 1999 to 2007 under Olusegun Obasanjo. He founded the American University of Nigeria in Yola, Adamawa State, and has long said his wealth comes from legitimate private business interests. He has repeatedly blamed Tinubu's policies, including the way fuel subsidy removal was handled, for rising prices. Tinubu's Rivers visit follows his trip to Akwa Ibom on Friday, where he said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, whose Rainbow Coalition backs the President, is a key ally in Rivers, and Governor Siminalayi Fubara has also declared support for Tinubu.
## Atiku replies

Later on Saturday, Atiku hit back in a statement issued by his campaign spokesman, Phrank Shaibu. He said his investment in education began long before he entered public office, when he laid the foundation for ABTI Academy in 1993, which later grew into the American University of Nigeria. In the same statement he referred to a 1993 US court forfeiture involving funds in an account linked to Tinubu, a matter the President's supporters have long said was a civil case that did not involve any criminal conviction. Atiku also said Tinubu's policies had pushed millions of Nigerians into extreme poverty, and rejected the President's claim that the economy is being rescued.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027, and campaigns by all the major parties are expected to intensify in the coming weeks.
more: Tinubu spoke at an APC rally in Port Harcourt.
He said he was cleaning up a mess left by Atiku and others.

stories.h: One dead, five injured as violence hits NDC rally in Asaba
stories.p: Delta police say one person died and five were injured in a clash during an NDC rally in Asaba on Saturday, after suspected thugs were filmed smashing supporters' vehicles. Police say organisers ignored advice to avoid a road procession.
body: Tension broke out at a rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State on Saturday, 7 November 2026, after suspected thugs were reportedly filmed destroying vehicles belonging to party supporters.
## What happened

Footage shared on social media appears to show a group of men vandalising vehicles at or near the rally venue. According to reports, some NDC supporters retaliated after the attack, raising tensions further. It is not clear who the attackers were, how many vehicles were damaged or whether anyone was hurt. The police had not publicly commented on the incident at the time of writing.
## Police confirm one death

The Delta State Police Command later confirmed that one person died and five others were injured in a violent clash during the rally in Asaba, which was held in support of the NDC presidential candidate. Police spokesman SP Bright Edafe said the violence happened on Nnebisi Road at about 12.15pm. The command said it had received intelligence before the event that violence was possible, briefed the organisers and advised them to hold the rally at an approved venue rather than on the road, but that the procession went ahead. The injured were taken to hospital and an investigation has begun. Police Commissioner Samuel Erale condemned the violence and urged all parties to avoid road processions and inform the police before political gatherings. The identities of the victims had not been released.
## Background

The NDC is the party of presidential candidate Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. Delta is governed by Sheriff Oborevwori, who joined the APC and has backed President Bola Tinubu's re-election. Political violence has already been reported on several sides ahead of the January 2027 elections: Obi's convoy was attacked in Calabar earlier this week, stones were thrown at a stage during a governor's campaign rally in Nasarawa, and APC supporters were attacked and a campaign vehicle burnt ahead of a rally in Katsina State last week. INEC has also warned of a plot to threaten and kidnap election workers.
## How people reacted
Many social media users condemned the violence and expressed concern for the safety of supporters at political events, while some warned that the same thugs could be used to disrupt the elections.
more: Suspected thugs reportedly destroyed NDC supporters' vehicles.
Some supporters were said to have fought back.
Police have not commented.

stories.h: Oyedepo warns politicians: 'The evil you don't stop will stop you'
stories.p: Bishop David Oyedepo has criticised the government over kidnappings and attacks on churches, warning politicians that evil left unchecked will consume them and telling anyone with a plan to Islamise Nigeria to drop it.
body: Bishop David Oyedepo, founder of Living Faith Church Worldwide, has issued a strong warning to Nigeria's political leaders over insecurity in the country.
## What he said

In a video shared on Saturday, 7 November 2026, the cleric questioned whether kidnapping and shooting people in churches could ever be considered anything but evil. He warned politicians that the evil they fail to stop will eventually stop them, urging those in authority to take responsibility for the country's security problems. He also said any plan to Islamise Nigeria should be abandoned immediately.
## Background

Oyedepo is one of Nigeria's most influential church leaders. His comments came a day after he led the dedication of Pastor David Ibiyeomie's 120,000-seat Hand of God Cathedral in Port Harcourt. Nigeria has faced persistent insecurity, with attacks by armed groups and kidnappings in many parts of the North and Middle Belt, including recent attacks on communities in Kaduna, Niger and Plateau states. Allegations of an agenda to Islamise Nigeria are regularly raised by some Christian leaders and rejected by the government, which says the violence affects people of all faiths.
## How people reacted

Many of his followers praised the bishop for speaking out, with some saying he was one of the few senior pastors willing to criticise political leaders openly. The government had not responded to his comments at the time of writing.
more: Oyedepo condemned kidnappings and attacks on churches.
He warned that unchecked evil will stop politicians.
He told anyone planning to Islamise Nigeria to drop it.

stories.h: Bobrisky says leaving Nigeria was one of the best decisions of their life
stories.p: Crossdresser and socialite Bobrisky says relocating from Nigeria two years ago was one of the best decisions ever made, describing the country as toxic and full of daily drama, and saying life abroad is peaceful.
body: Socialite Idris Okuneye, known as Bobrisky, says leaving Nigeria was one of the best decisions of their life.
## What Bobrisky said

In an Instagram post on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Bobrisky described Nigeria as a toxic environment where a new drama, piece of gossip or fight springs up every day. The socialite said life since relocating had been peaceful and that they would not give up that peace.
## Background

Bobrisky left Nigeria in November 2024 after a public row with the federal government over claims about the conditions under which a six-month jail sentence for abusing the naira had been served. The sentence was handed down in April 2024 after Bobrisky pleaded guilty to spraying and mutilating naira notes. Allegations that the socialite had served part of the sentence outside prison led to a government investigation and a dispute with activist VeryDarkMan, who first raised the claims. Bobrisky was stopped at the Seme border while trying to leave the country in October 2024 before eventually relocating.
more: Bobrisky left Nigeria in November 2024.
The socialite called Nigeria a toxic environment.
Bobrisky served a jail term for naira abuse in 2024.

stories.h: Wike and his Rainbow Coalition raise eyebrows as minister appears visibly angry at Rivers campaign ground
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike was reportedly seen checking how many people each of his aides had brought to the presidential campaign ground in Rivers State, looking far from pleased. The turnout has become a talking point, and so has the old question of paid crowds.
body: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike and his Rainbow Coalition campaign have got people talking again, this time after he appeared visibly angry at the presidential campaign ground in Rivers State.
## Counting heads

Wike was reportedly seen checking how many people each of his aides had brought to the venue. Photos show the minister, in his black and red hat and a rainbow "Coalition" sash bearing the APC logo, deep in conversation with aides and looking far from amused.
One can only feel sorry for any aide who collected mobilisation money and failed to deliver the expected crowd.
## The turnout question
The expectation may have been a stadium filled to capacity, but the turnout has now become a talking point on social media.
That brings us to Peter Obi, whose supporters often describe his campaign crowds as organic, with people attending out of personal conviction rather than financial inducement.
## Can anyone fill a stadium for free?

Crowd mobilisation, from buses to refreshments to small payments, has long been a feature of Nigerian political rallies across parties. Large crowds make for impressive pictures, but they do not always reflect how people will vote.
So one question remains: can any Nigerian politician genuinely fill a stadium without spending money on crowd mobilisation?
Nigerian politics will never stop surprising us.
more: Wike was reportedly seen checking how many people each aide brought.
He appeared visibly angry at the campaign ground.
The turnout has become a talking point online.

stories.h: "Fubara, you will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive": Tinubu assures Rivers governor
stories.p: At his presidential campaign rally in Rivers State, President Bola Tinubu gave Governor Siminalayi Fubara a strong personal assurance that he will not regret his decision. The remark has set people talking about what the governor did and what the President may have promised in return.
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has given Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara a strong personal assurance, telling him he will not regret the decision he has taken.
## What Tinubu said
"Fubara, you will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive," the President said during his presidential campaign rally in the state.
Photos from the rally show Fubara smiling beside FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, both wearing red caps bearing Tinubu's image, a striking picture given the long-running feud between the two men.
## Why the words matter
The statement is attracting attention because of the political tension that has surrounded Rivers State and the long-running power struggle between Governor Fubara and his political opponents.

For anyone who has followed Rivers politics closely, those words carry real weight. Fubara has faced some of the toughest political battles of his administration, with fights over political loyalty, control of the state legislature and the influence of powerful figures shaping events in the state.
## A sacrifice, a deal, or a new understanding?

With the President offering such a personal assurance, questions are being raised. The President did not spell out exactly what decision he was referring to, or what he intends to do for the governor in return.

Was Tinubu acknowledging a major political sacrifice by Fubara? Was he reassuring him over a difficult decision? Or could this signal a new understanding within the political leadership of Rivers State ahead of 2027?
## Over to you
What do you think Fubara has done, and what do you think the President has in store for him?
more: Tinubu told Fubara he would not regret his decision.
He spoke at his campaign rally in Rivers State.
Fubara and Wike appeared side by side at the rally.
stories.alt: President Bola Tinubu speaking at the Rivers rally, beside a photo of Nyesom Wike and Governor Siminalayi Fubara smiling in red caps

stories.h: DNA samples taken from Mohbad's remains and son Liam under court supervision
stories.p: DNA samples have reportedly been collected from the remains of the late singer Mohbad and from his son, Liam, in a court-supervised exercise in Lagos, after his widow, Wunmi, applied for a test to settle questions about the boy's paternity.
body: DNA samples have been collected from the remains of the late singer Ilerioluwa Aloba, known as Mohbad, and from his young son, Liam, as the long-running dispute over the child's paternity moves towards a resolution.
## What happened

According to reports on Saturday, 7 November 2026, the exercise took place on Saturday, 31 October, under the supervision of a Lagos court. The court had approved an application by Mohbad's widow, Omowunmi (Wunmi) Aloba, for a DNA test to establish Liam's paternity, and appointed a welfare officer to oversee the process. Samples were first taken from the singer's remains at the Mainland General Hospital in Yaba, then escorted under tight security to the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre, where Liam's samples were also collected.
## Who was present

The exercise was reportedly carried out with heavy security because of concerns about possible crowds. Mohbad's mother, his younger brother and his widow were present. The results have not been made public.
## Background

Mohbad died in Lagos in September 2023 at the age of 27. His death led to protests, a police investigation and a coroner's inquest. Since then, his father, Joseph Aloba, has repeatedly called for a DNA test on Liam, which led to a bitter public dispute with Wunmi and divided the singer's fans. The singer's death has also been at the centre of this week's public feud between VeryDarkMan and Davido.
## What happens next
The results are expected once the forensic analysis is complete.
more: Samples were collected on 31 October under court supervision.
The test was requested by Mohbad's widow, Wunmi.
The results have not been made public.

stories.h: US strikes Iranian air defence site as Trump insists 'we are not at war'
stories.p: US forces struck an Iranian air defence site on Qeshm Island on Friday, the second round of strikes this week, hours after Washington offered up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear programme. Trump described the strike as minor.
body: US forces struck an Iranian air defence site on Friday, 6 November 2026, the second round of American strikes on Iran in a week.
## What happened

President Donald Trump told reporters the operation was minor, saying Iran had built an anti-aircraft device and US forces destroyed it in a matter of minutes. He insisted the United States was not at war with Iran, pointing to the absence of recent US casualties. Iranian state media reported two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, close to the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for the world's oil shipments. Earlier in the week, on Monday, US forces carried out strikes that Washington described as defensive, with explosions reported on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam and near the naval hub of Bandar Abbas.
## Reward offer

Hours before Friday's strike, the US State Department offered up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear programme, including its scientists, technology and the organisations involved.
## Talks

Trump said Washington remained in contact with Tehran. Regional officials said Iran was considering new proposals brokered by Qatar to ease tensions, but that it would not negotiate over its nuclear programme until the US met several conditions, including lifting sanctions and ending a blockade of Iranian ports.
## Why it matters

Trump acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's losses in this week's midterm elections, partly because it pushed up petrol prices. Tensions in the Gulf can also affect global oil prices, which matter for Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs.
more: It was the second round of US strikes this week.
Trump called the strike minor.
The US offered $20 million for nuclear information.
